title: St John's wort tincture
subtitle: A long-course tincture of Hypericum perforatum for mild low mood
excerpt: St John's wort tincture is a 1:5 extract of fresh or dried Hypericum perforatum flowering tops in 40% spirit, taken daily for 6 to 8 weeks. Traditionally prepared in European herbal practice for mild low mood and the low-grade sadness of darker months. A 100 ml bottle holds about 20 doses and keeps two years in a dark cupboard. St John's wort has significant interactions with many prescription drugs, read the precautions carefully before using.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), St John's wort entry, Botanical.com. Cochrane review: Linde K et al., St John's wort for major depression (2008), Cochrane Database Systematic Reviews. EMA Scientific Opinion on St John's wort interactions (2012).

glossaryTerms.definition: A substance that speeds up the liver enzymes that break down drugs and other compounds. St John's wort is a potent CYP450 inducer, it lowers the blood levels of many prescription drugs, sometimes enough to make them ineffective.

projectSchedule.title: Start maceration
projectSchedule.body: Weigh 20 g of dried St John's wort flowering tops into a clean jar. Pour over 100 ml of 40% spirit. Seal and label with the date.

projectSchedule.title: Check and stir
projectSchedule.body: Check the herb is still submerged. The liquid should have turned a deep ruby red. Swirl and reseal.

projectSchedule.title: Strain and bottle
projectSchedule.body: Strain through muslin into a dark glass bottle. The finished tincture should be a deep translucent red. Label with the herb, spirit percentage, and date.

content.text: St John's wort herbal extract is a deep ruby-red extract of dried St John's wort flowering tops steeping in 40% spirit for 4 to 6 weeks. Traditionally prepared in European herbal practice for mild, persistent low mood, the dull, flat feeling that is not acute depression but makes the ordinary feel harder than it should. Taken daily for 6 to 8 weeks at a consistent dose. The Cochrane review found extracts of St John's wort superior to placebo for mild to moderate depression, with a side-effect profile similar to standard antidepressants. However, St John's wort has serious interactions with many prescription drugs, this is the herb that requires the most careful check of interactions before use.

attrs.title: Drug interactions, read before using
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

content.text: Weigh 20 g of dried St John's wort flowering tops into a clean steeping jar. Pour 100 ml of 40% spirit over the herb. Seal and label with the date.

Store in a cool dark place for 4 to 6 weeks, shaking every few days. At two weeks the liquid will have turned a striking deep ruby-red from the hypericin and pseudohypericin. This colour is the visual marker that the extraction is working.

3 to 5 ml in a small glass of water, twice daily. Take consistently for 6 to 8 weeks before assessing the effect, this herb does not act immediately. If you see no benefit at 8 weeks, consult a herbalist or doctor about alternatives.
Sealed dark glass bottle in a cool dark cupboard. Keeps two years from the date of straining.
When not to use this remedy

Do not use for severe depression, suicidal thoughts, or depression with psychotic features. These require urgent medical assessment. Do not take alongside prescription medication without checking with your prescriber, see the interactions list above. St John's wort is right for mild, persistent low mood in a person taking no prescription drugs. it is not right for moderate or severe depression.
